name: DNA double helix
headline: diameter
subtitle: B-form DNA, the common form in cells
description: DNA carries genetic information as two strands wound around each other in a right-handed double helix. The paired bases are stacked in the middle like the steps of a spiral staircase, with the sugar-phosphate backbones on the outside. In the common B form the helix is about 2 nm across, and it makes one full turn roughly every 3.4 nm along its length.

measures.label: Diameter
measures.note: Width of the double helix, stated as 20 Å (2 nm)

measures.label: Diameter (fibre model)
measures.note: 20.4 Å for B-DNA from optimised fibre-diffraction parameters (Arnott and Hukins 1972), as listed by BioNumbers; converted from Å

measures.label: Length of one helical turn
measures.note: One complete turn holds about 10 base pairs; stated as 34 Å

measures.label: Spacing between base pairs
measures.note: Stacked base pairs are 3.4 Å apart along the helix axis

facts.text: Each complete turn of the B-DNA helix contains about 10 base pairs.
In solution, water bound to DNA makes its apparent (hydrodynamic) diameter larger, about 22 to 26 Å.

sources.title: The DNA Double Helix - BIOC*2580: Introduction to Biochemistry (John Dawson)
Diameter of DNA double helix - BNID 105243

caveats: Both sources give the width in angstroms (20 Å and 20.4 Å), a unit not in the site's list; the Guelph text itself also states 2 nm, while 2.04 nm is an exact conversion of 20.4 Å. Turn length and base spacing are likewise converted from 34 Å and 3.4 Å.
Only the helix width is shown; a DNA molecule's length depends on how many base pairs it has, so no single length is given.
